newsitem.title: USA: Equitable Resources forms new subsidiary.
newsitem.headline: Equitable Resources forms new subsidiary.

text.p: Equitable Resources Inc said Thursday it launched a new, non-regulated subsidiary, ERI Services, designed to create and deliver energy solutions to businesses seeking to improve energy efficiency while reducing costs.
ERI Services also will offer commodity brokering of all forms of energy, including electricity and natural gas, the company said.

"Energy customers are beginning to demand lower cost and more specialized energy solutions than ever before," said Fred Abrew, Equitable's president and chief executive officer. "ERI Services is preparing us to effectively compete in the deregulated energy marketplace."

ERI, based in Pittsburgh, will employ about 200 people and have offices throughout the United States. The subsidiary combines employees and customers of Equitable's previously announced acquisitions of Independent Energy Corp and Conogen Inc.
The subsidiary will account for 5 percent of Equitable's revenues at the end of the year. It's expected to account for 25 percent by the year 2000.
The subsidiary will tailor products to meet customers' individualized energy needs and budget, from production to transmission to storage to total energy management.
